verses.1: And Joseph fell before his father’s face, and he wept over him.
verses.2: And Joseph commanded his servants and the doctors to anoint their father. And the doctors anointed Israel.
verses.3: And it lasted forty days. In this way, the days of the captivity continued. Then, the people of Egypt bowed down to him for seventy days.
verses.4: And as the days passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s officials, saying, “If I have found favor in your eyes, then please listen to me.”
verses.5: My father said to me, “Look, I am dead in my grave. I have made this grave for myself in the land of Canaan. Now, please let me rise up and bury my father.”
verses.6: And Pharaoh said, “Come up and bury your father, as you were commanded.”
verses.7: And Joseph went up to bury his father. All the servants of Pharaoh, as well as all the elders of Egypt, went with him.
verses.8: And all of Joseph’s household, along with his brothers, and his father’s household, only left in a state of despair. They abandoned their homes and went away into a land of desolation.
verses.9: And he brought with him also chariots and soldiers. Thus, the camp became extremely magnificent.
verses.10: And they came to the Jordan River, which is located across from the valley. There, they built a very large and magnificent temple. They also built an altar for their father, which lasted for seven days.
verses.11: And the Canaanite ruler saw the tree in the garden of Aton. He said, “This is a beautiful tree!” So he named it “Ablum.” But the Egyptians called it “Mizraim,” which means “over the river.”
verses.12: And his sons did as he commanded them.
verses.13: And his sons brought him down to the land of Canaan. They buried him in the valley of Hebron, the place where Abraham had purchased the land from Ephron, the Hittite.
verses.14: And Joseph, together with his brothers and all his kin, went to bury their father after he died.
verses.15: And the people of Joseph saw that their father had died. They said to him, “Yosef, please comfort us. Please restore all the harm that has been done to us.”
verses.16: And he commanded Joseph to say, “Your father commanded this before his death.”
verses.17: Thus said they to Joseph: “Please forgive the sins of your brothers and their transgressions. For they have done wrong to you. Now, please forgive the sins of the servants of your father’s God.” Then Joseph listened to what they said.
verses.18: And their brothers also went along with them. They fell down before him and said, “Let us serve you as your servants.”
verses.19: And Joseph said to them, “Do not be afraid. For I am God’s servant.”
verses.20: And you think evil of me, but God thinks well of me. This is so that I can create a great people today.
verses.21: And now, do not be afraid of me. I will eat you and your crops. Then I will comfort you and speak to you from the depths of my heart.
verses.22: Josiah sat in Egypt. He also lived in his father’s house. Josiah lived for one hundred and ten years.
verses.23: And Joseph saw Ephraim as being the descendants of thirty men. Also, Manasseh, son of Machir, was born to them, on the land of Joseph.
verses.24: And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dead. May God take care of you and bring you up from this land to the land that was promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
verses.25: And Josue blessed the children of Israel, saying, “May God punish you, and may He bring me down from this place.”
verses.26: Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They buried him in Egypt.
